Option 1: "در جهان مُلک سخن راندن مسلم شد مرا - نیست اقلیم سخن را بهتر از من پادشا"

Rough translation: "In the world, the kingdom of speech (or discourse) has become my Muslim (i.e., I have become a follower?)" Hard. So concept: claim of superiority in speech, authority, perhaps about mastery of words, governance of speech.

Option 2: "تا در سر خود کرد آخر سر خویش - بگماشت بالی تاج بر کشور خود"

Translation: "Until in his own head he made the end of his own... (maybe) He placed a wing (or crown) on his own country." Could be about self-sufficiency, self-rule, personal authority, putting a crown on one's own land. Theme of self-governance, authority.

Option 3: "که منم طاووس علیین شده - پس برآمد پوستش رنگین شده"

Translation: "Because I am a peacock that has become lofty? Then its skin became colorful." Something about being a peacock, proud, beauty, perhaps self-glorification, transformation.

Option 4: "امروز همه روی زمین زیر پر ماست - بر راستی...". "Today all the earth's surface is under our wing (or feather) - on truth ...". Something about dominance over earth, perhaps claiming power.

But let's double-check: Option 3 mentions "I am a peacock, then its skin became colorful." Could also be about transformation, beauty, perhaps about pride. Others talk about ruling, kingdom, crown, wing over earth. So yes, 3 is different.
